hints: Focus on how properties change as you go down a group, both for metals losing electrons and for halogens sharing electrons.
Compare Mg with Ca for first ionisation energy. The smaller atom higher up the group holds its outer electrons more tightly.
Compare Cl-Cl with Br-Br for bond energy. The smaller atoms form a shorter, stronger covalent bond, then pair that Group 2 metal with that halogen as $\text{MQ}_2$.
walkthrough:
**Pick the Group 2 element**

Think about first ionisation energy down Group 2. As you go down, the atom gets bigger and the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so it is easier to remove.

First ionisation:
$$\text{M(g)} \rightarrow \text{M}^{+}(\text{g}) + e^{-}$$

**Mg has the higher ionisation energy**

Magnesium is above calcium in Group 2, so Mg is smaller with less shielding. That means more energy is needed to remove its first outer electron.

Trend: $$\text{1st IE (Mg)} > \text{1st IE (Ca)}$$

**Pick the Group 17 element**

Now think about Q-Q bond energy. Bond energy generally decreases down Group 17 because the atoms get larger and the bonding overlap gets longer and weaker. So $\text{Cl-Cl}$ is stronger than $\text{Br-Br}$.

Trend: $$\text{Bond energy (Cl-Cl)} > \text{Bond energy (Br-Br)}$$

**Combine to get the formula**

We need Mg plus Cl. Group 2 metals form $2+$ ions ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$) and halogens form $1-$ ions ($\text{Cl}^{-}$), so we need two chlorides to balance the charge.

Formula: $$\text{Mg}^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2$$

options.A: Correct. Mg is higher than Ca in Group 2 so it has the higher first ionisation energy, and Cl-Cl has a higher bond energy than Br-Br. Combining $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ with two $\text{Cl}^{-}$ gives $\text{MgCl}_2$.
options.B: Incorrect. This correctly picks Mg for Group 2, but picks the wrong halogen. Br-Br bond energy is lower than Cl-Cl bond energy because Br atoms are larger with longer, weaker overlap.
options.C: Incorrect. This correctly picks Cl for Group 17, but picks the wrong Group 2 metal. Ca is below Mg, so it is larger and more shielded, giving it the lower first ionisation energy.
options.D: Incorrect. This gets both trends backwards. Ca has the lower first ionisation energy and Br-Br has the lower bond energy, so this is the opposite of what is asked for.
